author: Independent education critic subagent (claude-opus-5-5); did not author the reviewed artifacts

findings.claim: Activity 2 depends on an untaught API form. The pipeline uses the three-argument Collectors.groupingBy(classifier, mapFactory, downstream) with TreeMap::new, and the A-versus-B discrimination (key order) turns entirely on what that middle argument does. No course topic teaches the map-factory overload: grouping-with-streams-and-optional teaches only groupingBy(classifier, downstream) with counting and mapping (its only 'map factory' text is runtime JavaScript), and TreeMap::new appears on no other learner page. The page and the coverage plan state this page adds no new syllabus, and the recap (line 611) presents 'the map factory decides key order' as something retrieved.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence of teaching to Activity 2 before the code, for example: 'groupingBy also has a three-argument form; the middle argument is a constructor reference such as TreeMap::new that chooses which kind of map holds the groups.' Tie it explicitly to method-references (ArrayList::new) and choosing-the-right-collection (TreeMap sorts keys). Alternatively record the overload as a deliberate small extension in topic.json and the coverage plan instead of claiming no new syllabus.

findings.claim: Semantic answer leak. The Recap and Cheat sheet are rendered on the page at all times (only the activity sections are hidden by the script; the recap sits under the activity navigation), while the page tells learners to 'Answer from memory first'. The cheat sheet copies the correct answers in the page's own scenario: line 629 is the exact Activity 3 correct option 'toMap(Ticket::customer, Ticket::minutes, Integer::sum)'; line 626 is the exact Activity 2 grouping pipeline; lines 618-623 give ArrayDeque push/pop, ArrayDeque offer/poll and TreeMap, which is Activity 1's correct option C. Recap bullets at lines 610-613 restate the same decisions. A learner who scrolls once can answer all three checks by matching text.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the cheat sheet in a neutral domain with different identifiers (for example Order::region, Order::cents) and generic forms (keyMapper, valueMapper, mergeFunction), so nothing matches an option string verbatim. If the shared runtime allows it, keep the recap and cheat sheet hidden until data-pep-complete is true. Either way, no option text should appear verbatim outside its own fieldset.

findings.claim: Activity 3's only hint does the diagnosis for the learner. 'Ask whether it counts tickets, keeps one ticket's minutes, still fails, or adds the minutes' matches the four options one to one (A counts, C keeps one, B still fails, D adds). With the intended result 'Ana 50' already on the page, the clue amounts to 'pick the one that adds'. Objective o3 asks the learner to diagnose the collector, and a hint must not supply the classification.
findings.recommendation: Split this into two escalating hints that do not describe the options. Hint 1: look at 'attempted merging values 30 and 20' in the exception and say what single value Ana should end with. Hint 2: for each option, ask whether toMap still receives two values for one key with nothing told what to do with them, and if it does get told, what it does with them. Do not enumerate the four outcomes.

findings.claim: In Activities 1 and 2 the two hints split the problem into separate parts (Activity 1: hint 1 covers needs 1-2 and hint 2 covers need 3; Activity 2: hint 1 covers groupingBy and hint 2 covers the last pipeline). They do not build on each other, so a learner still stuck on needs 1-2 after hint 1 gets no further help from hint 2. Hint 2 of Activity 1 (line 415), together with 'sorted keys' in Where this fits (line 394), also nearly states the property that separates option C from B, leaving only a lookup of the class name.
findings.recommendation: Make each sequence escalate on the same reasoning. Activity 1: hint 1 asks the learner to name the order each need requires (newest first, oldest first, alphabetical); hint 2 asks which deque end each method touches and which map keeps a sorted order, without the contrast wording. Activity 2: hint 1 covers both key order and order within each list; hint 2 covers the Optional chain.

findings.claim: The page does not duplicate the existing review page, which covers HashSet choice, the equals/hashCode rule, ConcurrentModificationException, stream reuse, Optional.get and loop-to-stream rewriting. But two of its three 'new cross-topic scenarios' are close copies of topic checks. Activity 1 repeats choosing-the-right-collection's sorting practice ('Undo history, last action first: ArrayDeque'; 'Word counts printed alphabetically: TreeMap') and its GIFT task-queue item ('ArrayDeque, used with offer and poll'). Activity 3 repeats grouping-with-streams-and-optional's check ('one total per customer' via toMap with an adding merge function) and its GIFT o3 items (keep first, keep last, throws, adds with Integer::sum). That is recognition rather than the new transfer the course owner asked for.
findings.recommendation: Raise transfer in at least one of these activities. Activity 1: add a competing constraint such as a cost trap (also look up a waiting ticket by id) so the learner must trade off order against lookup cost. Activity 3: ask for a different per-key policy, such as each customer's longest ticket or the earliest-level ticket, so the learner has to derive the merge function rather than recognize Integer::sum. Keep the help-desk thread.

findings.claim: Companion mismatch. topic.json records artifacts.md status 'present', but the learner directory collections-streams/course-review/collections-and-streams-review-scenarios/ contains only artifact.html. So the required text alternative, and the static interaction alternatives it should carry (html-artifact-contract section 12), do not exist for learners who need them.
findings.recommendation: Generate artifact.md from the HTML with the contract's deterministic exporter and commit it. Otherwise set md to absent with an honest reason, but review topics normally carry HTML and Markdown, so generating it is the right fix.

findings.claim: The feedback for Activity 3 option A is incomplete. The option changes only the .collect(...) call, and the teammate's declaration is still Map<String, Integer> minutesPerCustomer. groupingBy(..., counting()) produces a Map<String, Long>, so the line would not compile. The explanation ('Ana would get 2 ... values would be Long counts') suggests it runs and returns 2.
findings.recommendation: Reword: 'Not quite. counting() produces Long counts, so this does not even compile against Map<String, Integer>; and if it did, Ana would get 2 tickets, not 50 minutes.'

findings.claim: Objective o1 says 'and justify each choice', but the check records only the chosen option. The justification appears only as an unobserved success criterion (line 422, 'You can name the order guarantee...'). So the objective verb is not aligned with the check.
findings.recommendation: Either reword o1 to 'Choose the stack, queue and map implementations whose ordering and cost guarantees fit a described feature' (in topic.json and the HTML), or add a short observable justification step, such as a second MCQ asking which guarantee rules out LinkedHashMap.

findings.claim: The 'Where this fits' good-fit line is a procedure for the activity ('Pick from the guarantee: last in first out, first in first out, or sorted keys'), which maps each need to its guarantee. DESIGN.md asks the good fit to describe actual scale and purpose and to contain no answer to the activity. The decision and the database boundary are authentic; the good fit is not.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the good fit as context, for example: 'In-memory working state for one running app (an undo history, a session's waiting line, a report built from loaded rows), where the order rule is part of the feature.' Keep the database boundary.
